text: Peter is a voice assistant built for a school science exhibition. He listens through a microphone, turns speech into text with Whisper, thinks with a small local language model through Ollama, and speaks with the Piper voice engine.
The plan is for an ESP32 microcontroller to be Peter's body, handling the microphone, the speaker and Wi-Fi, while a laptop is his brain.
Peter's brain runs on an old Intel i5-6300U laptop with no GPU, so nothing needs a powerful server.
Peter does not need the internet. Speech recognition, the language model and the voice all run locally on the laptop.
Peter uses Whisper for speech recognition, the phi4-mini language model through Ollama for thinking, and Piper for his voice.
If something fails, Peter can still answer common questions from a prewritten list of instant answers, so he does not go silent.
